clue.text: During cruise, loveless beauty appears most vulgar

indicators.note: During puts the shortened beauty inside the word for cruise, as something happening within it

parts.note: to cruise is to coast, moving along with little effort

indicators.note: loveless asks for the zero-shaped letter, love in tennis scoring, to be dropped

parts.note: a beauty, as in an English rose, is a rose

explanation.surface: On a holiday cruise, a heartless beauty behaves in the coarsest way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' drops the O (love, zero in tennis scoring) from the flower word, and 'During' puts what is left inside the cruise word.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse means crude or vulgar, so its superlative is the crudest of all.

clue.text: Shell suit

explanation.definitionFit: A case is a protective outer casing, and a lawsuit brought before a court is also a case.

clue.text: Passage from saga, untold relation

indicators.note: Passage from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An excerpt from a long saga tells of a family member whose story was never told.
explanation.definitionFit: A father's or mother's sister is a family relative.

clue.text: Rocket transporting poet, a drama

indicators.note: transporting means the rocket word carries the poet inside it

parts.note: to rocket is to soar, rising fast
Alexander Pope was an English poet

explanation.surface: A space rocket carries a poet aloft, which makes for a real drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet is Alexander Pope, an English poet of the 1700s; 'transporting' sets him inside the rocket word, with A tacked on at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running serial television or radio drama about everyday lives.

clue.text: Ultimate in cleaners, chars polish off awards

indicators.note: Ultimate in picks the final letter of the word cleaners
off signals the letters of chars and polish are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The best of the cleaners, the chars, polish off all the prizes.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a British word for a cleaning woman. 'off' rearranges CHARSPOLISH into CHOLARSHIPS, after S from the end of 'cleaners'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarships are grants or prizes given to students for merit.

clue.text: Spoil mog lying back beside me

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: lying back says the cat word is laid out in reverse order

parts.note: mog is British slang for a cat, a puss

explanation.surface: A cat lounging beside me spoils things.
explanation.walkthrough: Mog is everyday British slang for a cat; 'lying back' turns the cat word round before it joins on after ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To mess up is to bungle or ruin something.

clue.text: Tree climbed to collect a message

indicators.note: to collect means the turned tree word gathers the letter inside it
climbed in a down clue means the tree word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a lime is a kind of tree, the linden

explanation.surface: Someone climbs a tree to fetch a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbed' reverses LIME to EMIL in this down clue, and 'to collect' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic note sent over the internet is a message.

clue.text: To fail or succeed: to flounder — or to be a flounder?

definitions.text: to flounder — or to be a flounder?

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means everything depends on effort; flounder as struggle or as a flatfish gives sinking and swimming.

clue.text: God takes a month to beat pompous potentate

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
Jan is short for January, a month
to drum is to beat repeatedly

explanation.surface: A deity spends a month beating his drum, like some pompous ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A panjandrum is a self-important official or grandee.

clue.text: Involving northern English city, prosecute, so lie exposed?

indicators.note: Involving means the word for prosecute wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action against
Bath is a city in Somerset, England

explanation.surface: Someone is charged over a northern English city and left exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a spa city in south-west England. 'Involving' makes the legal word wrap round the north abbreviation and the city.
explanation.definitionFit: To bask in the sun is to lie with the skin exposed to its rays.

clue.text: Sound rule for big gun

indicators.note: Sound says the word for rule is spoken, giving a word that is said the same way

parts.note: a canon is a rule or principle

explanation.surface: A sensible rule governs the use of a large gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannon is a large artillery weapon, literally a big gun.

clue.text: Medium or small practice is absorbed by mine

indicators.note: absorbed by means the practice and is are taken into the mine word

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
a ritual is a customary practice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medium, or a small habit, gets swallowed up by a mining operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' looks like a size beside 'small', but it is the definition: a psychic. 'absorbed by' places the practice and 'is' inside the mine word.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium claims to contact the dead, a practitioner of spiritualism.

clue.text: Wonderful thing, look! A collection of animals drink everything in turn!

parts.note: lo is an old word for look

indicators.note: in turn says the run of words before it is read from end to start

parts.note: a zoo is a collection of animals
to lap is to drink like a cat
all means everything

explanation.surface: An excited cry at a zoo where the animals all take a drink one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' reverses AZOOLAPALL to LLAPALOOZA, which follows LO.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollapalooza is American slang for an outstanding person or thing.

clue.text: American's very angry over free Spanish outfit

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first pieces above the last one

parts.note: in American speech real is used to mean very
mad means angry
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: An American is furious at some loose Spanish garments.
explanation.walkthrough: Real Madrid is a Spanish football club. 'over' puts REAL and MAD above RID in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A football club is a team, which can be called an outfit; this one is from Madrid.

clue.text: Bird that wakes one up in the morning, twice? That is ridiculous

parts.note: the cock crows at dawn, waking people

indicators.note: twice means the morning abbreviation appears two times running

explanation.surface: A bird that crows two mornings in a row is absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockamamie is American slang for crazy or silly.

clue.text: Run away east, north or south, toward the west?

indicators.note: toward the west in an across clue means reading leftwards, backwards

parts.note: a pole is either the north or south pole

explanation.surface: Fleeing east, north, south, then west, in a panicked escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toward the west' reverses EPOLE in this across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run off secretly to marry.

clue.text: Settlement of ruler said to be made rustic

indicators.note: Settlement of means the letters of ruler and said settle into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ruler's settlement is said to have become a country village.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruralise is to make something countrified.

clue.text: Mortgage finally kept in check over antiquated housing agreement

indicators.note: over in a down clue sets the first pieces above the last one
kept in means the letter is held inside the restraint word

parts.note: a leash is a check or restraint

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of the word Mortgage

parts.note: old means antiquated

explanation.surface: A mortgage kept in check by an old-fashioned housing agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the last letter of Mortgage, 'kept in' holds it inside the restraint word, and 'over' stacks that above the antiquated word in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A leasehold is a tenure of property held under a lease for a fixed term.

clue.text: Willingly dig out hollow on tree

parts.note: to dig something is slang for to like it
an ash is a tree

indicators.note: hollow means the word out is emptied, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone digs out a hollow in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dig' is slang for enjoy, not excavate. 'hollow' empties the word out down to its first and last letters, which come after the tree, as 'on' places them.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something at once and eagerly, without hesitating.

clue.text: Twenty-seven states having passed bill, one left, making this?

definitions.text: Twenty-seven states having passed bill, one left, making this?

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a bill
I is the Roman numeral for one
the EU had twenty-seven member states

explanation.surface: The European Union passes a bill and a member state leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having passed' places the European Union after the bill and the one. Read whole, the clue pictures a member leaving the bloc and bidding farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French for goodbye, said by someone leaving.

clue.text: A different view of a murder plot is reinforced

indicators.note: different view of signals the letters of a murder plot are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Seeing a murder plot from another angle reveals something toughened.
explanation.definitionFit: Armour-plated describes something protected by steel armour.

clue.text: Suss out calm hearts as normal

indicators.note: hearts asks for the central letters of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Working out how to stay calm-hearted is the normal thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearts' takes US from Suss, U from out and AL from calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual means customary, as is normally the case.

clue.text: Unstoppable red tide unseats Tory from throne

indicators.note: unseats means the politician is turned out of the throne word

parts.note: throne is jokey British slang for a toilet, a lavatory
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political tide sweeps a Conservative from the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party. 'unseats' removes TORY from LAVATORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten rock from a volcano flows red and cannot be halted.

clue.text: Stuff one river into another

indicators.note: into means the river letter is placed inside the other river

parts.note: the Cam is a river in Cambridge, England
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Fill one river with another.
explanation.definitionFit: To cram is to pack or stuff tightly.

clue.text: Row behind America

parts.note: a rump is a behind, the backside

explanation.surface: An argument behind America.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy disturbance or quarrel.

clue.text: What's long gone is around, is around!

indicators.note: the second around signals the letters of is around are turned round into a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation that something long gone is back around again.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'is around' is the fodder and the second 'around' the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinosaurs died out millions of years ago, extinct.

clue.text: Work on river, fathoms down?

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the first piece after the second one

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
to ply is to work at a trade

explanation.surface: Working on a river, how far down?
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Scotland and also one in Wales; 'on' puts the work word after the river in this across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something many fathoms down lies a long way below the surface.

clue.text: The way fraud is treated, mafia leader finds place to breed

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: is treated means the letters of fraud are processed into a new order
leader picks the first letter of mafia

explanation.surface: A mafia boss treats fraud as a way of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is treated' rearranges the letters of fraud, set between the street abbreviation and the mafia leader's initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud farm is where horses are kept for breeding.
